mainTopic: Two answers to a contradiction in רבי יהודה's view on ביטול (nullifying one liquid in another), and רבא's summary of the three ways a mixture is judged: by taste, by majority, and by appearance.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא found a contradiction in רבי יהודה's view. In the משנה, he says the מי חטאת in a bucket dipped in a מקוה are nullified once most of the water is from the מקוה. But in a ברייתא, he says white wine mixed with water is not nullified. The first answer is that one ruling is רבי יהודה's own view, and the other repeats his teacher רבן גמליאל, who held that a liquid is not nullified by the same kind of liquid. רבא gives a different answer: the bucket was impure only on the outside, so by Torah law any bit of water is enough, and the stricter rule is only a rabbinic safeguard. רבא then sums up the three ways to judge a mixture: by taste, by majority, and by appearance. Next the גמרא notes that רבי אלעזר disagrees with ריש לקיש's earlier view, holding that forbidden items do not cancel each other, just as מצוה items do not. The source for the idea about מצוות is הלל, who ate the קרבן פסח, מצה and מרור wrapped together.

steps.title: One ruling is רבי יהודה's own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two rulings come from two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling is his own, and that ruling is his teacher's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction it just raised. One ruling is רבי יהודה's own view, and the other is a view he was reporting from his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה rules that the מי חטאת are nullified by a majority. That is his own opinion. In the ברייתא, he rules that white wine is not nullified, and there he is only repeating his teacher רבן גמליאל, who is strict when a liquid is mixed with the same kind of liquid. So there is no real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullification: one substance losing its identity in a larger amount of another

phrases.english: This one is his own
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה's ruling, where the מי חטאת get cancelled out by a majority.

phrases.english: that one is his teacher's.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the white wine ruling in the ברייתא, which comes from רבן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different speakers: one ruling belongs to the student, the other to his teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings are רבי יהודה's own, so he seems to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is רבי יהודה's own view; the ברייתא repeats רבן גמליאל's view.

steps.title: Proof that רבן גמליאל holds same-kind liquids do not cancel each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה reports in the name of רבן גמליאל that a liquid is not nullified in the same kind of liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבן גמליאל that blood does not nullify blood, spit does not nullify spit, and urine does not nullify urine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה really did report a strict view from his teacher רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבן גמליאל holds that a liquid cannot be cancelled by the same kind of liquid. That matches the strict ruling about white wine. It also shows that רבי יהודה is the one who passes along רבן גמליאל's teachings, which supports the answer in step 1.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says
in the name of Rabban Gamliel:
Blood does not nullify blood,
spit does not nullify spit,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מֵי רַגְלַיִם מְבַטְּלִין מֵי רַגְלַיִם.
phrases.english: and urine does not nullify urine.

steps.whatToRemember: First answer: רבי יהודה himself allows nullification by a majority, while his teacher רבן גמליאל holds that the same kind of liquid does not cancel itself.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer given in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה reports a strict view from רבן גמליאל, under which the same kind of liquid is not nullified.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה in the name of רבן גמליאל about blood, spit and urine.

steps.title: רבא: the bucket was impure only on the outside
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: in the משנה only the outside of the bucket was impure, so by Torah law any small amount of water is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: we are dealing with a bucket that is pure on the inside and impure on the outside. By Torah law, any amount of water at all is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different way to settle the contradiction. He explains that the bucket in the משנה needs very little to become pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the outside of the bucket was impure, so by Torah law the inside does not need to be purified at all. The מי חטאת inside therefore never really blocked the purification. That means the משנה is not a true case of nullifying a liquid, and it does not clash with the white wine ruling.

phrases.english: Rava says:
with a bucket whose inside is pure
and whose outside is impure we are dealing;
for by the strict law, any amount at all is enough for them,
phrases.notes: He means any amount of מקוה water reaching the bucket is enough by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בִּדְלִי שֶׁתּוֹכוֹ טָהוֹר וְגַבּוֹ טָמֵא עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction answered in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the משנה is about a bucket impure only on the outside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה relies on nullifying the מי חטאת by a majority, which clashes with the white wine ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law the bucket barely needs any water, so the משנה does not depend on real nullification.

steps.title: Why חכמים required more, and why a majority is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the stricter requirement is only a rabbinic safeguard, and once a majority of מקוה water is in the bucket, nothing more is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is חכמים who made a decree here, in case the person wants to spare the water and not nullify it. But once there is a majority of מקוה water, nothing more is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his answer. He explains why חכמים demanded a full immersion, and why a majority of water is enough to satisfy them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים worried that the owner would want to protect his precious מי חטאת, so he might dip the bucket carelessly and not let the water reach everywhere. That is why they required a proper immersion. Since this is only a rabbinic rule, once most of the water in the bucket is from the מקוה, the worry is gone and no more is required.

phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who decreed regarding them
lest he want to spare them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the precious מי חטאת in the bucket.

phrases.english: and not nullify it;
but once there is a majority, it is not needed.

steps.whatToRemember: Second answer (רבא): the bucket needs very little by Torah law. The stricter rule is only a rabbinic safeguard, and a majority of מקוה water satisfies it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a majority always cancels a liquid. Here the majority only matters because the extra requirement is rabbinic to begin with.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הוּא דִּגְזַרוּ בְּהוּ דִּילְמָא חָיֵיס עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer by explaining the rabbinic layer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Torah law versus rabbinic law: the majority rule applies only to a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A majority is needed because the מי חטאת must be nullified by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a rabbinic decree is involved, so a majority of מקוה water is enough.

steps.title: רבא's three rules for judging mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רבא sums up: a mixture can be judged by taste, by majority, or by appearance, and he explains when each one applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: חכמים spoke of taste, of majority, and of appearance. A substance mixed with a different kind is judged by taste. A substance mixed with its own kind is judged by majority. Where you can see it, it is judged by appearance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a general rule that sums up the laws of ביטול. He lists three ways to judge a mixture and says when each one is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two different kinds, you check whether the taste of one can still be noticed (טעם). With the same kind, taste cannot tell them apart, so you go by the majority (רוב). If the substance can still be seen in the mixture, like a liquid with its own color, you go by appearance (מראה).

keyTerms.meaning: A substance mixed with its own kind
A substance mixed with a different kind

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Rabbis said: by taste,
and the Rabbis said: by majority,
and the Rabbis said: by appearance.
A type with what is not its type: by taste,
a type with its own type: by majority,
where there is something visible: by appearance.

steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to judge a mixture: different kinds go by taste, the same kind goes by majority, and anything you can still see goes by appearance.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic framework for the whole topic of ביטול, used throughout the laws of mixtures.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section with a general summary of the rules of nullification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different kinds are judged by taste, the same kind by majority, and a visible substance by appearance.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Forbidden items do not cancel each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי אלעזר disagrees with the earlier view. He holds that, just like מצוות, איסורין do not cancel each other out.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: Just as מצוות do not cancel each other out, forbidden things also do not cancel each other out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי אלעזר that argues with the view that different forbidden foods cancel each other in a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view (ריש לקיש) held that when different forbidden items are mixed, one can cancel the other. רבי אלעזר disagrees and compares איסורין to מצוות: when two מצוה items are combined, neither one wipes out the other. In the same way, each forbidden item keeps its own status.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees, meaning this opinion argues with another one
Cancel out (nullify), so the item loses its own status in a mixture
Here: food items used to do a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a real argument about mixtures of different forbidden foods, and it ties that argument to how מצוה foods behave.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: The view he's arguing with is ריש לקיש's earlier one, that forbidden items cancel each other out.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Elazar said:
Just as מצוות do not
nullify one another,
so too prohibitions do not
nullify one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא returns to ריש לקיש's earlier view that forbidden items cancel each other, and notes that רבי אלעזר disagrees with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden items do not cancel each other out, just as מצוה items do not cancel each other out.

steps.title: Who holds that מצוות do not cancel each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier authority holds that מצוה items do not cancel each other out, since רבי אלעזר built his rule on that idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one we heard saying that מצוות do not cancel each other out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the idea רבי אלעזר relied on. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר compared איסורין to מצוות, so his rule only works if someone really holds that מצוות do not cancel each other. The גמרא wants to find the earlier authority behind that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard? This is the גמרא asking which authority holds a certain view

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מִצְוֹת מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ?
phrases.english: מצוות do not nullify one another?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the comparison רבי אלעזר made in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which authority holds that מצוה items do not cancel each other out.

steps.title: It is הלל, who ate the פסח, מצה and מרור together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is הלל. A ברייתא says he wrapped the קרבן פסח, מצה and מרור together and ate them at once, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is הלל. A ברייתא teaches: They said about הלל הזקן that he would wrap them together and eat them all at once, because the פסוק says: "With מצות and מרורים they shall eat it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the view that מצוות do not cancel each other comes from הלל, and it proves this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the strong taste of the מרור cancelled out the מצה, then eating them together would ruin the מצוה of מצה. Since הלל ate them together, he must hold that one מצוה food does not cancel out the other. That is the idea רבי אלעזר relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herbs eaten on the night of פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: just as מצוה foods eaten together (like הלל's wrap) do not cancel each other out, different forbidden foods do not cancel each other out either.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not mainly about the סדר. The גמרא brings it only to show that הלל held that one מצוה food does not cancel another.

phrases.english: It is Hillel,
as it was taught in a baraisa:
They said about Hillel the Elder
that he would wrap them together at once and eat them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the meat of the קרבן פסח, the מצה, and the מרור.

phrases.english: because it is stated:
"With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by naming הלל and bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל holds that מצוות do not cancel each other, since he ate the פסח, מצה and מרור wrapped together.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about הלל הזקן, based on במדבר 9:11.
